senses.gloss: pr. n. pl.Cæsarea, name of several cities, esp. Cæsarea (Palestina), a maritime city founded by Herod the Great on the site of Straton’s Tower.
units: <cite ref="Megillah 6a:12">Meg. 6ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>עקרון</he>, <cite ref="Zephaniah 2:4">Zeph. II, 4</cite>) <he>זו ק׳ בת אדום וכ׳</he> this means (symbolically) C., the daughter of Edom (seat of the Roman government) &c., v. <cite ref="H00323"><he>חוֹל</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Zephaniah 2:4">Ib.</cite> <he>מלכי ק׳ וירושלים</he> the governors of C. and of Jerusalem.
<cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 4:24">Lam. R. to IV, 21</cite> ‘daughter of Edom’ <he>זו ק׳</he> this means C.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Ohalot 18:16">Tosef. Ohol. XVIII, 16</cite> <he>ק׳ שהחזיקו בה וכ׳</he> C. which was always considered unclean (v. <cite ref="M00273"><he>מָדוֹר</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Tosefta Ohalot 18:13">Ib. 13</cite> <he>מזרח ק׳</he> the eastside of C.; Ohol. XVIII, 9 (ed. Dehr. <he>קסרון</he>, corr. acc.; some ed. <cite ref="S01087"><he>קֵיסַרִיּוֹן</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 3:7:6">Y. Pes. III, end, 30ᵇ</cite> <he>רבנן דק׳</he> the Rabbis of C.; a. fr.—
Y. Yeb. II, end, 4ᵇ, a. e. ק׳ שבקפודקיא Cæsarea in Cappadocia, v. מְגִיזָה. Mekh. B’shall., Amal., s. 2 קסריון, v. מְחִלָּה.—Denom. קִיסְרִי, קִסְ׳ Cæsarean.

<cite ref="Tosefta Demai 4:23">Tosef. Dem. IV, 23</cite> <he>הניח ק׳ ומצא אגרי</he> (Var. <he>ומצא עִגְּרוֹן</he>) if he left Cæsarean wheat (bought for immediate use) and found storage wheat in its place (v. <cite ref="A00282"><he>אֵגוֹרִי</he></cite>).
